artifact_revision: agentmux 98a4ff75 + session-15 working tree (amx 0.8.0, revision 98a4ff7516c2-dirty, built on the Studio and copied; Agent Mux.app Debug built on the MacBook Pro from the synced working tree, run as a copy under bundle identifier io.github.sglavoie.agentmux.acceptance15); embedded Ghostty 1.3.1; tmux 3.7c (a relocated copy, AgentMux's private server); Claude Code 2.1.296, codex-cli 0.162.0, Copilot CLI 1.0.95; macOS 27.0.1 on the MacBook Pro
method: One recorded live run, from a fresh world, of nine cases in order (fresh claude codex copilot history link ime priority reattach): 190 checks, 0 failed (interaction-acceptance.log ends 'RESULT: 0 check(s) failed'). TWO MACHINES, by the operator's rule that no UI runs on the Studio. Everything seen and driven is on Seb's MacBook Pro: the app copy and its window, tmux, the world's daemon and registry (isolated under /tmp/amxs15 there, no Kitty), every key, pointer event and picture. The driver runs on the Studio and only sends: scripts over SSH to read state (tmux formats and screens, the registry, the daemon's v2 snapshot, the app's unified log, the link target's log, the clipboard), and input through a headless VNC client (driver/vnc.py; no viewer window), which is real screen-sharing input to the MacBook's console. Three kinds of input do not survive screen sharing and were posted as real HID events on the MacBook over SSH instead (driver/hid.swift, private event source, modifier state checked 'none' after use): wheel turns, the keys typed into the input method, and the global shortcut. The three harnesses are real and signed in on the Studio only; each runs there headless in a pseudo-terminal and its terminal is carried over SSH into the tmux pane AgentMux launched for it on the MacBook (driver/bridge.py, which also carries the pane's TERM/TMUX identity). So a session has two process identities, both checked: the pane process on the MacBook, which is what AgentMux registered, and the harness process on the Studio. The pane program first sends one managed SessionStart hook to the world's daemon so the session is listed; the harness itself never sees the AgentMux identity. A fourth session, 'history', is a stand-in line printer on the main screen (3000 lines and a link) so that tmux, not a harness, holds its history. Earlier full passes are not the record: one had 2 failed checks that were the driver's (a screen capture read where the copy-mode cursor was meant; a browser fetch expected from a browser that was not running), one stopped on a driver fault in the attention step, and partial passes found driver faults that were corrected (the bridge did not carry the pane's terminal identity, so Claude took Shift+Return as Return; a composer-clearing helper sent Codex its quit key). Temporary changes on the MacBook, all with the operator's approval and all reverted and verified: /Library/Preferences/com.apple.RemoteManagement VNCAlwaysStartOnConsole was absent, was set to true so the shared-password viewer joins the console instead of a login-window session of its own, and is absent again ('read again: absent'); /usr/libexec/sshd-keygen-wrapper was added to Privacy & Security > Accessibility so SSH-launched processes may post events, and was removed (afterwards 'accessibility trusted: false can post events: false'); the Japanese input method was enabled and disabled again with the enabled list compared before and after ('restored'); the world, the app copy's preferences and /tmp/amxs15 were removed. Not reverted: the MacBook's clipboard was overwritten by the copy and paste checks; a macOS prompt 'Allow Python to find devices on local networks' was answered Don't Allow. NOT exercised: a person at a physical keyboard, trackpad or mouse; drag and drop; middle-click paste; OSC 8 hyperlinks; selection made by a harness's own mouse handling (a plain drag inside a full-screen harness); Option-modified keys; the Release build; a browser actually loading the link (the MacBook's default browser was not running: it was started for the link, stopped at its own profile chooser, and was closed again). Automated checks beside the live run: go-test-tmux.log (internal/tmux viewer, wheel, mouse-binding and attach tests against a real tmux, and the root test tying the app's history requests to tmux's user keys) and mac-test-remote.log (the hosted suite run on the MacBook through macos/scripts/remote-ui.sh: 347 tests, 0 failures).

claude-interaction-matrix.evidence: Observed in session-15/interaction-acceptance.log (case 'claude: interaction matrix', 27 checks, 0 failed), through the app copy's embedded terminal on the MacBook Pro with the real claude harness (process on the Studio, pid 19614, its terminal bridged into the tmux pane whose process is MacBook pid 48713). A real click on its sidebar row attached exactly one terminal and the pane took the viewer's 107x39 grid. Keyboard: typed text reached the composer; Control+A and Control+E moved to the start and end of the line; Shift+Return made a new line with the two lines one above the other and nothing submitted; the composer was cleared with Control+U and Backspace; Return submitted a prompt and the 150-line answer reached 'S15MARK 150'. Paste: Command+V pasted two lines and the line break submitted nothing. Scrollback: the harness draws its own full screen with the mouse on (tmux history 0), so its transcript is its own; a real wheel turn scrolled it back and forward, and Shift+Page Up / Shift+Page Down (View > Page Up/Down) paged it to the first lines and back (8 presses down), all without entering tmux's copy mode. Selection and copy: Shift+drag over a line then Command+C put exactly 'S15MARK 149' on the clipboard. Find: Command+F opened tmux's find over the screen, landed on the typed text, and Escape returned to the live screen. Mouse: a plain click and a right click left the same pane process and the same harness running. Input method and links for this harness are under 'ime' and 'durable-history-search'. Pictures: session-15/claude-matrix.png, session-15/claude-selection.png.

ime.evidence: Observed in session-15/interaction-acceptance.log (case 'a real input method composes at the cursor', 26 checks, 0 failed), for each of Claude, Codex and Copilot. With the macOS Japanese input method (Kotoeri romaji) selected in the MacBook's GUI session, the keys k a were posted as real key events: the composition was drawn underlined at the composer's cursor and the agent's screen held neither か nor 'ka' (session-15/ime-claude-composing.png, ime-codex-composing.png, ime-copilot-composing.png); Return committed it, the agent's composer then read か, and nothing was submitted. A second composition (n i h o n n) was held back the same way and, on Return, arrived converted: each composer read か日本 (ime-*-committed.png). Back on the original layout a plain key typed plainly (か日本z) and nothing was submitted. Afterwards the MacBook's enabled input sources were identical to before ('restored') and no modifier was left held. Why real key events: keys sent through screen sharing bypass input methods (seen while preparing the run: with the method selected, 'ka' typed through the viewer arrived as 'ka'), so these keys alone were posted on the MacBook itself. In-process coverage of the same path: GhosttyInteractionTests.testACompositionReachesTheProgramOnlyWhenCommitted and testACancelledCompositionSendsNothing in session-15/mac-test-remote.log.

shortcut-focus-priority.evidence: Observed in session-15/interaction-acceptance.log (case 'who gets a key depends on what has the keyboard', 21 checks, 0 failed). Session terminal focused: plain keys were Claude's. Command+D was the app's: the Dashboard view took the pane and Claude received nothing of it. Dashboard focused: '?' opened the Dashboard's own help and did not reach Claude (session-15/priority-dashboard.png). Command+Shift+] was the app's from the Dashboard too: it selected a session, focused its terminal, and typing then reached that agent. Command+Shift+L gave the keyboard to the session list: typing reached no agent, the Down arrow moved the selection to the next session while the keyboard stayed in the list, and Return went into that session, whose agent then received typing. Control+O reached Claude (its transcript view opened) and the app's Command+O Overview did not open. F12, tmux's detach key, detached the view (the app showed Detached, no client on the pane, the agent still running and never sent F12; priority-detached.png); the Reattach button attached again and the keyboard was back with the agent. The global next-attention shortcut (Control+Option+Command+N, posted as a real key event), pressed while typing to Claude, focused the session that a real PermissionRequest hook had marked as waiting, and Claude received nothing of the chord (priority-attention.png). The ownership rule itself (every menu shortcut holds Command except Shift+Page Up/Down; no key a program binds is the menu's) is asserted by WorkspaceShortcutTests in session-15/mac-test-remote.log.

durable-history-search.evidence: Observed in session-15/interaction-acceptance.log (cases 'history held by tmux' 21 checks, 'a link printed in a session' 5 checks, and the history steps of the reattach case; 0 failed). A main-screen program printed 3000 lines; tmux held 2964 of them as history. With no tmux key or prefix: Shift+Page Up entered the history and a second went a page further; Shift+Page Down to the bottom returned to the live screen; Command+Home reached the oldest line (position 2964 of 2964, cursor on 'LINE 0001 needle-0001'; session-15/history-top.png); Command+End returned; Command+F asked for text and landed on 'LINE 0042 needle-0042' (history-find.png); Command+G stepped to the match before and Shift+Command+G back; Escape returned to the live screen; a real wheel turn scrolled into the history and back out. A plain drag selected a line and copied it on release with no prompt ('LINE 2988 needle-2988'); Shift+drag then Command+C copied exactly 'LINE 2990 needle-2990' (history-selection.png); a right click did nothing, and no binding of the private server opens a menu or kills, respawns or splits a pane (history-right-click.png). Durable: after the window was closed and the app quit and started again (a different app process), tmux still held all the lines and Command+F in the new viewer found 'LINE 0007 needle-0007'. Link in the same session: Command+click alone went to tmux and opened nothing; Command+Shift+click made the app log 'opening a link with scheme http' and the MacBook's default browser was started for it (it was not running; it stopped at its profile chooser, so no page load was observed, and that instance was closed). For the three full-screen harnesses the history is each harness's own transcript in a process tmux holds, reached by the wheel and View > Page Up/Down and still complete after reattachment (see long-output-reattach); Find there covers the visible screen.

long-output-reattach.evidence: Observed in session-15/interaction-acceptance.log (case 'long output and reattachment', 29 checks across its three parts, 0 failed). Each real harness had produced a 150-line answer. Command+W closed the window: the app logged 'workspace: closed, detaching', no client remained attached to any pane, and each pane process (MacBook) and harness process (Studio) was the same with no viewer. The app was then quit and started again: a different app process (48861 then 64746). For Claude, Codex and Copilot in turn, a click on the row attached the new viewer to the same pane; the pane process and the harness process were unchanged (for Claude: MacBook pid 48713, Studio pid 19614); the end of the long answer was on screen again; Shift+Page Up still reached the first lines of the answer ('S15MARK 2'/'S15MARK 3' on screen) and Shift+Page Down returned to 'S15MARK 150'; and typing reached the same agent. The tmux-held history of the fourth session survived the same replacement with all its lines and was searched with Command+F from the new viewer (session-15/reattached.png). Earlier in the same run the detach key and Reattach button did the same for one session without closing anything (shortcut-focus-priority). All of it used only the app's menus and keys: no tmux prefix or tmux key.
